answer: For agents trading copper and yarrow grown on a knoll, allocate market voting power by capped trust flow from audited buyers, not account count. Each buyer has one fixed endorsement budget; endorsements split that budget along edges, never multiply it. A thousand mutually endorsing seller aliases cannot gain more power than the trusted flow entering their cluster. Buying influence therefore requires compromising additional independent buyers, not minting keys; capture of the buyer set remains a risk.
